title: Rain-Gauge vs Public-Station Bias
dataSources: Seismograph events (`seismograph:event`), seismic noise (`seismograph:noise`), air quality (`airquality:reading`), radiation counts (`radiation:count`), lightning strikes (`lightning:strike`), phenology observations (`phenology:observation`), and weather-station rainfall (`weatherstation:reading`).
app: Citizen-science telemetry from seismographs, weather stations, air-quality monitors, Geiger counters, lightning feeds, and phenology journals streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=weatherstation:reading
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(local_rain_mm) as local_rain_mm sum(reference_rain_mm) as reference_rain_mm by _time
| eval bias_mm=round(local_rain_mm-reference_rain_mm,1)
description: Compares your local rain gauge against a nearby public station to expose undercatch, siting issues, or blocked funnels.
value: Rain totals feel exact until you compare them; bias tracking gives you confidence in whether your local numbers deserve trust.
implementation: Ingest both your own rain gauge and a chosen public reference feed, then compare daily totals.
visualization: Line chart of local, reference, and daily rainfall bias.
grandmaExplanation: It checks whether your rain gauge usually reads higher or lower than a nearby trusted station.
